tagline: Back roads past a reservoir that took four towns.
intro: Route 122 leaves Orange and runs south through New Salem, Petersham, Barre and Rutland to Paxton, forty miles of back roads on the north side of the Quabbin Reservoir. In Petersham it crosses Turnpike Street, which was Route 21 before the reservoir took the valley the old road ran through.

Four towns were given up in the 1930s so the Quabbin could supply Boston. Hundreds of homes, a state highway, a railroad line and 34 cemeteries were moved or dismantled. Greenwich sat lower than its neighbors and is largely under water, except three hilltops, which are islands now.

moments.title: The Lookout, New Salem
moments.text: Behind the New Salem fire station an unmarked gravel road leads to a lookout over the reservoir, with Mount Wachusett to the east and Mount Monadnock in New Hampshire to the north.

moments.title: Dana Common
moments.text: Through Gate 40 the old road, closed to cars, leads on foot to cellar holes and a stone marker reading Site of Dana Common 1801-1938.

moments.title: Moore State Park
moments.text: Turkey Hill Brook drops 90 feet in 400 feet here, and it turned a gristmill and a sawmill as early as 1747, with a restored sawmill there now.
